rationale: This is a pure aggregator swap (MIN for MUL) on the identical two rank legs of the already-evaluated AccrualBuildupDecayingProfit, and since MIN and product of two uniform ranks are highly correlated, it is a cosmetic variant unlikely to yield economically new information.

Replacing TREND(...,5) with DELTA(...,2) on the same two legs of the archive's winning signal is a measurement-window tweak rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the coverage argument alone does not justify it as a new cross-theme hypothesis.

Internally consistent and economically distinct from the margin-decay archive signal, though both legs lean on well-documented anomalies (multi-year net-operating-asset/working-capital growth and Soliman-style asset-turnover changes), so the novelty rests entirely on the interaction rather than the inputs.

Sign conventions are handled correctly (NEG(invch) is genuine inventory buildup) and the obsolescence story is crisp, but it verges on rediscovering the Thomas-Zhang inventory-change component of the accrual anomaly conditioned on low sales growth, and the product will absorb a large low-growth main effect.

A genuinely under-explored non-working-capital accrual channel with a coherent conditional story and correct sign logic, though the multiplicative form leaves a strong margin-improvement main effect that typically predicts positive returns and could blunt or invert the expected negative slope — a difference-of-ranks or conditional form would test the interaction more cleanly.

The funding-source channel is a legitimate and untested angle that meaningfully repairs the weak payables/leverage idea, but multiplying two ranks that are each already known negative predictors (accruals and net debt issuance) means the signal will largely reproduce those main effects rather than isolate the claimed interaction.
